title: R&D Engineer - Adaptive Memory Management / Operating Systems
description:
À propos de l'offre d'emploi

R&D Engineer - Adaptive Memory Management / Operating Systems
Paris, France, Onsite, Fixed-Term Contract (CDD)

Join the R&D team of a global technology company working on next-generation computing and memory architectures. As an R&D Engineer you will research and develop C-based OS algorithms for adaptive memory management within distributed shared-memory architectures. The R&D Engineer will work across OS internals and hardware interfaces, designing experiments to evaluate new approaches and contributing to potential research publications. Open to strong MSc graduates from top French institutes as well as early-career engineers.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Develop adaptive memory-management algorithms within the OS using C.
- Interface OS software with hardware and internal OS structures.
- Work with distributed shared-memory architectures.
- Design experiments and analyse technical results.
- Contribute to research documentation and publications.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

Essential:
- BSc, MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electronics or related field.
- Strong C programming.
- Experience/knowledge of Operating System design and internals.
- Understanding of memory management, processes, IPC and concurrency.
- Knowledge of computer architecture and hardware/software interfaces.

Desirable:
- Distributed/shared memory or cache coherence experience.
- GEM5, SystemC, RTL or hardware experience.
- C++ and/or Python.
- Research experience and at least one first-author paper.

WHY APPLY?
- Work on next-generation many-core and memory architectures.
- Strong combination of OS, hardware and systems research.
- Opportunity to contribute to potential publications.
- Open to strong MSc graduates and early-career engineers.
- CDD initially through July 2027, with potential extension.
- Approx. €40,000–€50,000, depending on experience.

RECRUITER'S NOTE
Ideal candidates include OS Engineers, Systems Software Engineers, Embedded Software Engineers, Research Engineers and Computer Architecture Researchers with strong C and OS knowledge. Candidates from semiconductor, embedded, HPC or academic research backgrounds are particularly relevant. Memory management, shared memory, concurrency and HW/SW interface experience will stand out.

Apply now or send a copy of your CV, referencing the title and location, and with a short introduction to cw@eu-recruit.com.

ai_analysis.summary: Solid technical match (~70%): the candidate has extensive hands-on C/OS internals work (custom malloc, Linux kernel driver, namespace/cgroup-based container runtime, epoll server) and embedded/ASIC hardware exposure, directly aligning with the OS-and-hardware-interface core of this role. The main gaps are the absence of distributed shared-memory/cache-coherence experience and any research publication track record, both explicitly valued for this R&D position.
resume_tips: Explicitly add 'memory management', 'IPC' and 'concurrency' as keywords near your kernel/malloc projects — the job description uses these exact terms.
Highlight myMalloc and the RFID Linux kernel driver at the top of your project list since they best match 'adaptive memory management' and 'hardware interface' requirements.
Quantify the Arista work (e.g., number of ASIC register types handled, performance/latency gains from DMA changes) to show measurable R&D impact.
Mention any exposure to GEM5, SystemC or RTL simulation, even academic, since it's a desirable skill explicitly listed in the posting.
If you have any coursework, thesis, or write-up related to distributed/shared-memory systems or cache coherence, surface it — this is a stated gap versus the desirable criteria.

Reframe the container runtime (My Docker) description to emphasize 'OS-level resource isolation' and 'kernel internals' rather than 'container runtime' to better match ATS parsing for this OS-focused role.
ai_analysis.recommended_profile: Looking for a full-time position in software engineering with a focus on OS internals and adaptive memory management. MSc in Computer Engineering (EPITA - GISTRE) in Systems / Embedded. Fluent in French and English (TOEIC 915, C1). Interests: watchmaking, music, hiking/running, cooking.
